Read the methodology ↗
THE PRESSURE FILTER
TOP 20%

Relative to the match situation.

A delivery is high pressure when its pre-ball pressure score is in the highest fifth of its competition × innings × phase group.

Required run rateWickets lostBalls remainingKnockout stageChase closeness

First innings: late overs, lost wickets and scoring deficit. Chases: rate demand and a closeness factor that reduces the weight of nearly decided games. The same pre-ball flag applies to batter and bowler.

01 What do the card numbers mean?+

HP SR: 100 × runs ÷ balls faced in high pressure. HP economy: 6 × runs conceded ÷ legal balls; byes and leg-byes excluded. Ordinary: the same rate outside high pressure.

HP balls / matches: the sample behind the result. Top-10 checks: how many of 13 analysis versions selected the player in the top ten. The settings are explained below.

02 What does “13/13 checks” mean?+

A setting is one version of the analysis with a particular set of assumptions. We ran one baseline and twelve variations, ranking the same primary-eligible player pool each time.

  • 1 baseline: top 20% pressure, wicket value 12, pressure shrinkage 150 and ordinary-impact weight 0.20.
  • 3 pressure variations: top 25%, 15% and 10%.
  • 2 wicket values: 8 and 16 runs per dismissal.
  • 2 shrinkage values: 75 and 300 pressure units, varying the small-sample penalty.
  • 2 ordinary-impact weights: 0 and 0.40 instead of 0.20.
  • 2 pressure-formula variations: remove chase closeness; use alternative component weights.
  • 1 recency variation: older years weighted by 0.85 per year.

13/13 means top ten in all versions; 12/13 means top ten in twelve. For example, Kuldeep has 13/13 and Patidar has 12/13. Higher counts show less sensitivity to these assumptions. They do not count matches or guarantee future performance. The final order uses mean rank, not this count alone. On uncapped cards, main-list checks still refer to the original batting/bowling top tens, not selection within the watchlist.

03 How is the ranking calculated?+

Batting value = runs − 12 × dismissals. Bowling value = 12 × credited wickets − runs conceded. Each is compared with held-out peer expectations for competition, innings, phase and match context.

Pressure and ordinary residuals are shrunk towards zero for small samples. The primary score is 100 × (h − 0.2u − 0.5SEh), where h and u are shrunk pressure and ordinary residuals and SEh measures match-level uncertainty.

Final order uses the lowest mean rank across the 13 analysis versions (settings), with primary score breaking ties. The consensus index rescales that mean rank within the eligible pool; it is not a success percentage. Rounded indices may tie.

04 Who qualifies, and is comparison fair?+

At least 500 total balls, 120 pressure balls, 250 ordinary balls, 10 pressure matches and two calendar years. There are 70 eligible batters and 78 eligible bowlers.

Five whole-match folds separate peer estimation from player evaluation. Context includes IPL/T20I, innings, phase, season, role, opponent, venue, wickets and chase demand, using hierarchical smoothing.

05 What data was used?+

Six supplied CSVs connect delivery events to players, matches, teams, competitions and playing XIs. After strict Cricsheet supplementation of missing extras and exclusions, 166,227 of 200,999 events remain (715 matches, 22 Jan 2022–1 Nov 2026). Excluded share: 17.3%.

Only the match state before each ball defines pressure. Normalising pressure within competition, innings and phase makes the exposure comparable across roles.

06 Can Rajasthan Royals sign these players?+

This is a historical performance ranking, not a confirmed 2027 auction list. Role fit uses RR’s published 2026 squad as a reference. Acquisitions depend on release/trade, registration, clearance, budget and overseas balance.

Riyan Parag is existing RR core. Fakhar Zaman, Abrar Ahmed and Shaheen Afridi are benchmark-only profiles until IPL entry is verified. Mustafizur’s 2027 clearance needs specific verification.

07 How robust are the results?+

The 13 settings test changes in assumptions (see all versions); 1,000 whole-match bootstrap draws test sampling variation. These are separate checks. Bootstrap frequencies are conditional on the fitted model.

The 2026 holdout test shows weak persistence: rank correlations are −0.374 for batting (28 players) and −0.039 for bowling (29). The pre-2026 batting top ten underperformed other eligible batters in 2026. These rankings describe history and are not a validated 2027 forecast.

2026 HOLDOUT

Predictive limits

The 2026 holdout did not establish reliable predictive performance. Combine these rankings with current form, fitness, scouting and verified auction eligibility before recruitment decisions.

Availability evidence & source notes

The official IPL news feed was reviewed for 2027 squad movements and pool announcements. No final 2027 shortlist was verified in that review. Status must be rechecked before making recruitment claims.

Registration and final auction shortlisting are separate steps; see the official 2026 auction announcement for a documented example, not a 2027 availability list.

Historical rank does not establish availability: IPL confirmed Kuldeep Yadav’s move to LSG. His pressure ranking is therefore not treated as evidence that RR can bid for him.

Candidate eligibility, 2027 base prices, release decisions and clearance are unverified. The six cards are a research queue; any retained, traded, withdrawn or ineligible player must be excluded from an auction-only bid list.
